To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the transcriptional approach allowed to identify novel splicing defects in LGMD2A patients, (ii) the genomic characterization of a large‐sided deletion in CAPN3 allowed to identify a recurrent deletion and (iii) the transcriptional study provided evidence that some CAPN3 mutations are associated with nonsense‐mediated mRNA decay

1) the use of a complementary approach based on the transcriptional analysis allows to identify and characterize CAPN3 mutations that are difficult to detect by genomic analysis and 2) nonsense‐mediated decay of messenger RNA is a possible explanation for the under‐expression of the protein observed in patients with nonsense or frameshift mutations.

(1) transcriptional explorations of patients suspected to be affected with LGMD‐2A, who present only one CAPN mutation, can reveal novel CAPN3 splicing mutations, (2) a large‐sizing genomic deletion of CAPN3 can be identified and (3) the CAPN3 messenger RNA decay can be involved in some specific mutations

the characterization of novel splicing mutations in the CAPN3 gene and the identification of a large‐sied genomic deletion.

transcriptional analysis is a useful approach for the identification of CAPN3 mutations, particularly for those mutations located in intronic regions or in exons that are not routinely analysed.

transcriptional analysis of CAPN3 can be used to identify novel mutations, to determine the origin and size of deletions and to identify mutations that may lead to under‐expression.
